newsitem.title: UK: Quiet Bradys could gain from EMU confusion-analyst.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Bradys could gain from EMU confusion-analyst.

text.p: Brady bond prices hovered near overnight levels in extremely light trade on Thursday, emerging market traders said.
"The market is quite dead. Most of Europe is on holiday," an analyst said.
German, Austria and Poland are on Corpus Christi holiday, which Colombia and Venezuela will hold on Monday.

The analyst said the Bundesbank's rejection of the German government's plans to meet Maastricht criteria for entry to European economic and monetary union (EMU) by revaluing Germany's gold reserves, was causing confusion.
"The emerging markets have become a safe-haven of common sense versus European government bonds amid this confusion," he added.
But dealers said there was still not much news to move prices.

On Wednesday Brady bond experts said market participants would again start to look to key U.S. economic data to assess what the Federal Reserve's move might be at the next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting in July.
Among Eastern European debt instruments, Bulgarian FLRBs were unchanged at 51-5/8 bid and Russian Vnesheconombank dollar denominated loans were unchanged at 85-3/8 bid.
Brazilian IDUs were unchanged at 98-1/2 while Mexican pars were at 74-1/4 and Argentine pars were at 66-3/8 bid. -- Hayley Pienaar, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
